topic: Federated MCP Architecture: Distributed Security Boundaries for Multi-Server Fleets
title: Federated MCP Architecture: Distributed Security Boundaries for Multi-Server Fleets
lead: Connecting dozens of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers directly to a single Claude agent creates prompt bloat, security cross-contamination, and tool naming conflicts. Enterprise environments require an MCP gateway router to isolate server boundaries and enforce fine-grained access control.

stats.title: Enterprise Multi-MCP Telemetry:
items: Unfederated MCP setups expose an average of 42 distinct tools simultaneously, bloating context prefixes by 18,000 tokens before user input.
Federated routing gateways trim active tool schemas to strictly relevant sub-domains, cutting turn latency by 45%.
Granular tool namespaces eliminate cross-server command collision and unauthorized database access across tenant boundaries.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: API Gateway vs. Direct Microservice Exposure
mentalModel.text:
In cloud architectures, you never let single web clients open raw connections to internal database clusters, billing engines, and auth servers. You place an API Gateway (Kong, Envoy) in front.

Federated MCP acts as an Agent API Gateway: Claude connects to an MCP Gateway Router that dynamically surfaces only the tools needed for the active workflow step.

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: Never dump dozens of MCP servers into a single unnamespaced Claude configuration.
Implement namespace prefixes (e.g., github__, db__) to prevent tool collision.
Use dynamic tool filtering to include only contextually relevant tool definitions in prompt schemas.
takeaway.badge: Federated MCP routing turns chaotic multi-tool fleets into governed enterprise infrastructure.

topic: Graph Engineering & Knowledge Graphs with Claude
title: Graph Engineering: Why Vector RAG Fails on Multi-Hop Queries and How GraphRAG Solves It
lead: Vector similarity search finds direct text matches effectively, but cannot trace multi-hop relationships across interconnected entities. Graph engineering combines Neo4j knowledge graphs with Claude's structured reasoning.

stats.title: Vector Search Blindspots in Complex Systems:
items: Standard vector RAG accuracy drops below 28% on multi-hop questions (such as tracing upstream service dependencies to an expired SSL cert).
Graph-augmented LLM pipelines (GraphRAG) boost multi-hop relationship extraction accuracy from 34% to 89% while reducing context hallucinations.

mentalModel.title: 1. The 60-Second Mental Model: The Family Tree vs. A Bag of Words
mentalModel.text:
Vector search treats documents like a pile of post-it notes in a blender, locating notes with similar keywords. To find a second cousin twice removed, semantic similarity does not help; you need graph edge traversal.

Graph Engineering turns Claude into a Graph Query Engine: Claude generates Cypher queries, traverses relationships, and reasons over interconnected enterprise knowledge.

 subgraph RAG ["Vector RAG (Flat Similarity)"]
 Q["User Query"] -.-> V1["Chunk A"]
 Q -.-> V2["Chunk B (Missing Connection!)"]
 end
 subgraph GraphRAG ["Graph Engineering (Entity-Relationship)"]
 E1["Service A"] -->|DEPENDS_ON| E2["Database B"]
 E2 -->|HOSTED_IN| E3["VPC Us-East-1"]
 E3 -->|MANAGED_BY| E4["Team Security"]

 end
 style Claude fill:#1e3a8a,stroke:#60a5fa,color:#fff

diagramCaption: Figure: Flat Vector Embeddings vs. Connected GraphRAG Traversal
codeContent:
from neo4j import GraphDatabase
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

def generate_and_execute_cypher(natural_query: str, schema_description: str):
 prompt = f"""Translate this user question into a read-only Cypher query.\nSchema: {schema_description}\nQuestion: {natural_query}\nOutput only inside <cypher_query> tags."""
 response = client.messages.create(
 model="claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219",
 max_tokens=1024,
 messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}]
 )
 # Extract Cypher and execute against Neo4j read replica
 cypher = response.content[0].text.split("<cypher_query>")[1].split("</cypher_query>")[0]
 return db_driver.execute_query(cypher)

takeaway.title: Key Takeaways
items: Avoid relying solely on vector embeddings for relationship-heavy enterprise queries.
Extract entities and relationships into a graph database (Neo4j, AWS Neptune) during ingestion ETL.
Have Claude generate Cypher or Gremlin queries to perform structured path traversals.
takeaway.badge: GraphRAG bridges semantic similarity with deterministic relational logic.
